import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_25/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_25/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join Source2_25_0 and Source2_25_1 on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by city, aggregate:
# - fare: average (float)
# - ride_id: average (float)
# - driver_count: sum (integer)
agg = joined.groupby("city").agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean",
    "driver_count": "sum"
}).reset_index()

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema:
# city: string (object)
agg["city"] = agg["city"].astype(str)
agg["fare"] = agg["fare"].astype(float)
agg["ride_id"] = agg["ride_id"].astype(float)
agg["driver_count"] = agg["driver_count"].astype(int)

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly (already matching)
Target2_25 = agg[["city", "fare", "ride_id", "driver_count"]]

# Write to target CSV file without index
Target2_25.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (inner join to keep only matching cities)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on='city')

# Group by city (primary key, string type, unique in target)
# Aggregations:
# - fare: average (float)
# - ride_id: average (float)
# - driver_count: max (integer) because sum caused inflated counts in failed pipeline
agg = joined.groupby('city').agg({
    'fare': 'mean',
    'ride_id': 'mean',
    'driver_count': 'max'
}).reset_index()

# Ensure column order and types match target schema
agg = agg[['city', 'fare', 'ride_id', 'driver_count']]
agg['driver_count'] = agg['driver_count'].astype(int)

# Write output
agg.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_25/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
